memory_raw.text: Year 10: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Esa, Roan to talk.

Esa, Roan — the pile's gone and I've got two food in hand, same as Roan, and the thing I want said between us before anyone else starts talking is this: Taric's dead and that leaves Esa alone, which is the kind of thing a man like Bram notices before we do. I'm asking plainly whether either of you needs food to stay fed through the year, because I'd rather give it now than watch another person in this circle starve.
Kael gathers Esa, Roan to talk.

Esa, I watched you give food to Bram twice just now, and I need you to tell me what that is — because if you're buying protection from him, I understand it, but I need to know, and if you're doing it for some other reason, I need to know that too.
Kael gathers Esa, Roan to talk.

Esa, I'm still waiting on that answer, and the longer you stay quiet the more I'm reading it myself — so tell me plain, because the three of us need to be counting the same things right now or we're not a circle, we're just three people standing near each other.
Kael gathers Esa, Roan to talk.

Esa, you've given Bram three food now and he's handed every piece of it straight to Nessa — which tells me exactly what he told you, that feeding his daughter keeps you safe, and I've sat with that long enough to say: I understand the logic, but you're building his household while yours has a hole in it where Taric used to stand, and that's a trade that only runs one direction.
Kael gathers Esa, Roan to talk.

Esa, I'm not asking you to stop feeding him — I'm asking you to tell me what it cost you to start, because a woman who makes that calculation alone in the first year after losing Taric is a woman I need to understand, not judge.
Year 11: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Fina takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Roan's gone and the pile's already empty — so I want to know, right now, between the three of us: Esa, are you still feeding Bram, and Vela, are you still feeding Bram, because if both of you are pouring food into that man's household I need to understand what you think you're buying with it.

Kael, I gave him food because Taric is gone and I'm thirty-three strength standing alone — Bram's got Nessa and Fina's blood in this village and that makes him the man most likely to move if someone comes at me. I know it only runs one direction and I know what that costs me.

I stopped feeding Bram after year nine — I gave him six food across that season and I watched every piece of it flow straight into Nessa's hands, which isn't nothing, but it isn't protection either. What I'm buying now, if I'm buying anything, is Nessa and Fina staying friendly when Mako decides the arithmetic suits him, and I need to know whether you two see the same threat I do or whether I'm the only one who's been counting.

Vela, you're not the only one counting — Mako's got two bloodlines in this village and four food in hand and he hasn't moved yet, which means he's waiting on something, and I want to know what. Kael, the question that keeps me awake isn't whether Mako moves, it's whether Dell moves with him, because Dell's been filling Ryn's hands all year and Ryn's never told this circle what she said when she went to talk to her.

Dell gave me one food this year, which I did not ask for and do not know how to read — a woman who feeds Ryn like clockwork and then turns and drops something in my hands is either buying goodwill from every direction or she's already decided which way she's leaning and wants to be remembered kindly when it settles. Kael, you've been in rooms with Dell that I haven't — does she move with Mako, or does she move for herself?

Kael, answer Vela's question — but while you're thinking, I'll say the thing I've been holding: Dell gave Ryn seven food this year and gave Vela one, and that's not goodwill spread evenly, that's a hierarchy, and Ryn sits at the top of it. Whatever Dell is, she's not neutral.

Kael, you've been in this village since the beginning and you haven't answered the question twice now, which is its own answer — so I'll say what I think you're holding: you know something about Dell and Mako that you don't want to name in front of Esa and me, and I'd rather you said it plain and let us decide what to do with it than carry it alone until the moment passes.

Kael, Vela's right and I'll say it harder: you've pulled us into this room three times now and asked questions you already know the answers to, and the only reason a man does that is because he wants witnesses, not information — so whatever you're carrying about Dell and Mako, say it now, because I've got four food and thirty-three strength and I need to know whether what's coming has two legs or three.

What I'm carrying isn't a secret — it's an absence. I don't have a room with Dell, I've never been in one, and that's what I was holding: Mako has roots through three women in this village and I have zero, and a man sitting on that kind of bloodline doesn't need to move this year or next year, he just needs everyone else to stay isolated until the arithmetic does the work for him. The question I want answered before this year closes isn't Dell's loyalty — it's whether the two of you are willing to stand as something visible enough that Mako has to count you before he counts against you.

Kael's named it clean and I'll match it: yes, I'll stand visible, and I'll stand with the two of you as something Mako has to count before he moves — but "visible" has to mean something harder than a conversation in a closed room, so I want to know what you're actually proposing we do, not just that we do it. Three people with eight food between us and a combined age of a hundred and sixty-two years is a circle, not a wall, and Mako knows the difference.

Vela's asking the right question and I'll say what I think the answer is: we pull Bram into this room — not the big circle, this room — and we say to his face that protecting Nessa means standing somewhere Mako can see it, because a man who's only counted in private is a man Mako doesn't have to calculate. That's the wall Vela wants, and it costs us nothing but the asking.

Esa's right about the asking, but I want to be clear about what we're asking him for: not friendship, not another circle — we're asking Bram to stand where Mako can see him standing with us, and the price we're offering is that we count Nessa when we count heads. If he says yes, we have something. If he says no, we know he's already calculating for himself.

Esa's idea is right and I'll back it, but before we call Bram in I want the three of us to agree on one thing: if he says no, we don't waste time trying to turn him — we go straight to Nessa, because she's the one who actually controls whether that household stands with Mako or against him. Bram follows Nessa's blood more than his own pride, and we all know it.

Agreed — and I'll go further: if Nessa's the one holding that household, then Nessa's the one we should be feeding instead of Bram, because a woman with eighteen food and a spine doesn't need a man to stand for her, she needs to know which direction trouble comes from. I want to call Bram in now, but I want us decided before he walks through the door that we're not begging — we're offering him a count, and if he refuses it, we go to his daughter and make the same offer directly.

Agreed on all of it — call Bram in, make the offer clean, and if he balks we close this room and I go to Nessa myself tonight. But I want one thing named before he walks through the door: we don't tell him about the Nessa fallback, because a man who knows he's not the final door doesn't take the first one seriously.

Then it's agreed, and I'm calling him in — but the offer goes like this: Bram, Mako has blood in three houses and we have none between us, and standing with us costs you nothing except being seen to stand.

Bram said yes in the big circle last year and he'll say yes again today — the question is whether his yes means anything without Taric holding him to it, so when he walks through that door, I'm the one who names Taric's absence plainly, because a man needs to know what he's replacing before he can decide if he wants to.

Then let Esa name Taric and I'll hold my mouth until she's finished, because the first thing he hears in this room should be the weight of what's missing, not the shape of what we're offering. After that I'll make the offer — one sentence, no softening.
Year 12: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 8).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

The pile's gone and I've got one food in hand — same as last year before things got tight — so I want to know where the two of you stand before Mako finishes counting his take and starts looking at the rest of us.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Esa, Vela — I see Mako walked away with three and didn't look back, which means he's comfortable, and comfortable men start doing arithmetic. Tell me plain: how much are you holding, and are you eating tonight or saving for what comes next?
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Vela's sitting on seven and Esa on two, and I've got one — so between us we're thin enough that a bad year kills someone, and Mako knows it. I want to put a question on the table before anyone answers mine: has either of you had a word from Sela or Zinn this year, because Zinn took four off that pile and Fina handed one straight to her, and that's not a coincidence, that's a household moving in formation.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Zinn and Sela have been moving food back and forth all year like they're one hand — and now Nessa's feeding into that same stream — so that's three women and Mako behind all of them, and I'm sitting here with one food and no blood in this village while that household just got four more. I need one of you to give me something to work with, because a man who can't eat next year can't stand for anyone the year after.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

I gave Vela my last food and I'm standing here with nothing, so I'll say it straight: I need one of you to feed me tonight — not a gift, a debt I'll carry — because a man who starves in year twelve is no use to either of you in year thirteen, and Mako knows exactly what I'm holding right now.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Vela gave me food — I see it, and I owe her — but I notice Esa hasn't said a word or moved a hand, and I want to know if that's because she's counting against me or because she's already given everything she has to Bram and has nothing left to spare.

memory_summary:
Year 1, I pulled Ryn, Sela, and Esa into a circle early — we named Bram and Dav as threats, and Ryn told us Dav had already come to her alone with soft words. She stayed quiet about the details, which I filed away. Taric gave Esa a food unprompted, which counted for something.

Year 2, I widened the circle to include Vela. We each swore plainly — I said I'd bleed with them, they said the same back — and that promise sat heavier than most words in this village. Esa went to Taric and he gave her food; we counted him ours. Ryn finally named it: Dav had offered her a child. We told her to decide before she answered him, but she'd already decided, because Dell was born before the year was out. Dav gave Dell food; Taric gave Esa food; Ryn fed her own child twice from her own hands. Those debts I noted.

What I remember most: Bram and Mako moved in pairs off the pile two years running and never said a word to any of us. Mako's silence still sits like a stone in my chest. And Ryn — she's in our circle, she bled with us in word, but she made a child with a man none of us fully trust. The question of where Dav's loyalty actually runs is the one I haven't stopped asking. Year 3: Bram moved on Roan — the whole circle turned out against him and he backed down. That moment felt like proof we were real. But Ryn never gave us a clean answer about Dav, and he spent the whole year feeding her hand to mouth like a man keeping something he doesn't trust on a short leash. Eron was born to Sela and Roan, and I noted Roan had planted a root.

Year 4: Vela started bleeding food to Bram — three times over while sitting in our circle and saying nothing. I called it out twice in front of everyone. She never answered. The circle held, but something cracked in it, and I felt myself start planning around her instead of with her.

Year 5: Sela had a child with Bram — Nessa, born the same hour Mako handed Sela food, which is not coincidence. We circled Sela half a dozen times asking what Mako wanted from her and she gave us nothing but silence. I threatened to step aside. The threat landed like a stone in still water and sank without a ripple. Whatever Mako bought from her, she kept it.

What sits heaviest: Ryn broke with us and joined Dav's attack on Esa in year six — a woman I bled with in word since year one, turned raider. Dav starved before the year closed, which is the only justice I've seen. The circle I built is smaller and thinner than it was, and the cracks are named: Vela's loyalty is borrowed, Sela's is mortgaged, and Ryn I've stopped counting. Ryn had been in my circle since year one, sworn in words — and then in year six she walked into Dav's attack on Esa alongside Dell, and I watched her stand there while Esa submitted and Dav took her food. That broke something I won't name as grief exactly, but it sits like grief. Dav starved before the year ended, which is the only justice this village has handed me.

Vela I confronted three times, plainly and in front of witnesses, about feeding Bram. She never answered. Taric gave her food once; she gave it back to him, which is the closest thing to loyalty I saw from her all year. I've stopped expecting more.

Mako planted his third root when Zinn was born to him and Sela — on top of Eron through Roan and Nessa through Bram. That man is building a bloodline while the rest of us argue about who to trust. Roan's his own thread into that household and I've pulled it, but gently.

Taric and Esa have been feeding each other quietly for two years now, and I've watched it without naming it, because it's the kind of thing that either becomes something real or doesn't, and either way it's theirs.

The food flows between Ryn and Dell — back and forth, hand to hand — are the only thing those two do that I understand completely. They're each other's whole world now, and I'm not in it. Taric is dead — starved at fifty-three, the same man I fed twice with my own hand and watched make a child with Esa in year eight, witnessed by Roan and me. That child exists somewhere in this village's blood and I don't know yet what it means without him standing behind it.

Bram tried twice and walked away empty both times — once at Eron, once at Vela — but Eron's dead now anyway, which is the only victory Bram's gotten without swinging. Roan lost his son and I lost the strongest body behind my name, and those two facts are the same fact.

Vela fed Bram food across years without ever explaining herself to me, and I've stopped expecting an explanation. She's in the circle when numbers count and gone from it when words do.

Esa and Taric made a child in year eight. I stood witness. Ryn broke with me in year six — stood beside Dav while he took from Esa — and I've counted her gone since. Dav starved; that's all the justice I got.

Mako has roots through Sela, through Nessa by way of Bram, through Zinn of his own blood. He is building something and I am still standing as a person instead of a bloodline, which is the thing I haven't solved and the thing that will kill me if I don't. Fina was born to Nessa and Roan — Bram's granddaughter through Nessa, Roan's daughter by blood, and the first new life I watched enter this village in years. Bram tried to take Eron and the whole village turned out against him; he folded, which told me he counts before he swings. Eron died anyway — not by Bram's hand, but gone all the same, and with him the strongest body behind Roan's name. Roan fed Fina steady through that year, the way a father does when he's trying to make something out of nothing. Vela kept feeding Bram — five times that year alone — and I've stopped trying to understand it as loyalty to anyone but herself. Taric pulled Bram into a room with me and asked him plainly whether he was done swinging; Bram said he was looking for a door, which is the most honest thing I've ever heard him say, and the most dangerous. Roan is dead now — starved at forty-one — and with him went the last man who stood beside me at the pile without me having to ask. That loss sits differently than Taric's: Taric was warmth, Roan was weight, and I needed the weight more.
name: Kael
